title.narrative: ROAP/PHL Strengthening Institutions and Empowering Localities Against Disasters and Climate Change (SHIELD) Project

description.narrative:
The Strengthening Institutions and Empowering Localities Against Disasters and Climate Change (SHIELD) is a six-year Australia-DFAT-funded program that aims to support the government of the Philippines in building institutional and community resilience to climate change and other types of hazards.
The goal of the SHIELD Program is to make all people in target communities safer and more resilient to the impacts of natural hazard events and climate change. This will be realized by achieving three inter-dependent outcomes/components:
• Component 1: Government, private sector, and civil society stakeholders in targeted local government units (LGUs) are collaborating to unlock funding and implementing informed and inclusive resilience actions • Component 2: Relevant national government agencies (NGAs) are prioritizing action on local climate and disaster resilience • Component 3: Philippine scientific agencies are producing tailored and accessible information for local resilience action
In partnership with the Government of the Philippines, the SHIELD Project will be implemented by the UNDP, together with consortium partners, including UN-Habitat, Philippine Business for Social Progress, National Resilience Council, and the Consortium of Bangsamoro Civil Society. The Department of Interior and Local Government serves as the lead Government partner for the implementation of the SHIELD Program.
The SHIELD Program’s Theory of Change (TOC) rests on a core premise that all people in the target communities will be safer and more resilient to the impacts of disasters and climate risks if stakeholders at the national and subnational levels are effectively collaborating and jointly planning for collective outcomes; investing and acting together for building resilience, and measuring the impact of resilience-building actions.
Within the project framework, UN-Habitat will provide TA support to partner local governments as well national agencies involved in planning and investment programming for disaster and climate resilience. Mainly, UN-Habitat’s inputs will be for components 1 and 2 of the project. Specifically, it will lead or co-lead capacity-building tasks and activities centered on: building tools development and use; resilience planning workshops; resilience project structuring/development; thematic trainings; and policy development support including improvement of M&E and Learning schemes.
